title: You think God can’t use you after what you’ve done.
paragraphs: You think God can’t use you after what you’ve done.

But what if your worst moment…
is exactly where He starts?
Because the truth you’ve been avoiding is this—

It’s not your weakness that disqualifies you.
It’s your refusal to bring it into the light.
And deep down… you know it.

You replay it at night.
That decision.
That compromise.
That secret nobody else knows.

You smile in public…
but inside, there’s a quiet sentence echoing:
So you try to fix yourself.

Pray a little more.
Hide a little better.
Serve a little harder.
Because behavior modification can’t heal what only the blood of Jesus can cleanse.
But only the ones who stop pretending they’re not.
Face to face with pressure… he folded.

Walking with Jesus.
Seeing miracles.
Hearing His voice.
And still… choosing fear over faith.
And maybe that’s where you are.
But collapsing in areas you swore you’d already overcome.
Some of us don’t need more motivation.
Because secret sin doesn’t weaken your walk.

Proverbs 28:13 says:
“He who conceals his sins does not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.”
But God doesn’t heal what we keep hiding.
Because the story didn’t end with Peter’s denial.
After the resurrection, Jesus didn’t ignore him.

Back to the shore.
Back to the fire.
Back to the place of failure.

“Why did you fail Me?”
“Why weren’t you stronger?”
“Why did you mess up again?”
Because Jesus isn’t just after your behavior.
And with every “Yes, Lord…” Peter gave—
This same Peter who denied Jesus…

You are a sinner.
Not misunderstood.
Not just “going through something.”

Sin is real.
And it separates us from God (Romans 3:23).
But God didn’t wait for you to fix yourself.
Jesus Christ lived the life you couldn’t live—perfect, sinless, holy.
Then He died the death you deserved.

Romans 5:8 says:
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
While you were still in it.
Jesus didn’t just carry your sin.
Proving that sin doesn’t have the final word.
Shame doesn’t have the final word.
Your past doesn’t have the final word.
Still calling it “struggle” when deep down you know it’s surrender to sin?
To say what needs to be said—
You are not too far gone.
But you have to come into the light.

1 John 1:9 says:
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”

Not tired of you.
Not done with you.
Because sometimes the first step out of hiding…

And if this stirred something deep inside you—
don’t ignore it.
This is where grace meets truth.
This is where broken people get rebuilt.
